response.sql: SELECT AVG(rebrate / feerate) AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(*) AS fee_record_count FROM fees WHERE feerate > 0.0009;

assumptions.assumption: The count covers all fee records with feerate > 0.0009, including those with a NULL rebrate. Only the average skips NULL ratios, because AVG ignores them.
Because the filter is feerate > 0.0009, feerate is never zero or NULL in the rows used, so the division is safe.

alternatives.interpretation: Count only the fee records that have a non-null rebrate, so the count matches the rows that went into the average.
alternatives.sql: SELECT AVG(rebrate / feerate) AS avg_rebate_to_fee_ratio, COUNT(rebrate) AS fee_record_count FROM fees WHERE feerate > 0.0009;
